A.explanation: Work on the object is $W = 12 \text{ N} \times 0.0050 \text{ m} = 0.060 \text{ J}$ using its own upward displacement.

B.explanation: This uses the plunger displacement $4.0 \text{ cm}$ instead of the object displacement $0.50 \text{ cm}$: $12 \times 0.040 = 0.48 \text{ J}$.

C.explanation: This uses $0.50$ without converting $\text{cm}$ to $\text{m}$: $12 \times 0.50 = 6.0 \text{ J}$.

D.explanation: This uses $4.0$ without converting $\text{cm}$ to $\text{m}$: $12 \times 4.0 = 48 \text{ J}$.

hints: Notice the wording 'work is done on the object' - focus on the force on the object and the distance the object itself moves, not the $4.0 \text{ cm}$ plunger movement.
Recall $W = Fd$ for force parallel to displacement, where $F$ here is the $12 \text{ N}$ weight lifted slowly upward through $0.50 \text{ cm}$.
Convert the object displacement from $0.50 \text{ cm}$ to metres before multiplying by $12 \text{ N}$ to get joules.
walkthrough: Identify the object: weight $W = 12 \text{ N}$ acting downward, lifted slowly so the applied upward force equals $12 \text{ N}$.
Identify the relevant displacement: the object moves upward by $d = 0.50 \text{ cm}$. The $4.0 \text{ cm}$ plunger movement describes work done on the gas, not on the object.
State the rule: work done $W = Fd$ when force and displacement are in the same direction.
Substitute: $W = 12 \text{ N} \times 0.0050 \text{ m} = 0.060 \text{ J}$, with unit $\text{N m} = \text{J}$.
